description: Zwift's own monthly race series - a themed set of week-long stages each month, open to everyone. Every stage's route in one calendar, with the fastest bike and wheel combo worked out for each.
note: September is Zwift Racing Powered by DURA-ACE - four week-long stages, and the month ZRacing moves under Zwift's new Zwift Racing umbrella alongside Crit Club, Epic Race Club and TT Club events. The stages listed here are the ZRacing ones. Entry is by racing score - Women-Only, Range 1, Range 2 and Advanced - and every category rides the same course, so there is one bike answer per stage; GC is your best finishing time on each. August's Makuri Madness stages are below, completed. Later months are added when Zwift announces each theme.
curatorNote: Modelled as one season per calendar year, each month a round (round number = month number), weekly stages as races - a stage runs Monday to Sunday, so every race carries an endDate. Stage GC is by best finishing time, hence format 'scratch'. All four stage routes now carry generated surface data, so rankings run on measured composition and the pages show 'measured' confidence. Reading that composition: Zwift rolls sand at the same Crr as tarmac (0.004 on road wheels), so Makuri's long beach sections are free - a coarse 'off tarmac' percentage that buckets sand as gravel badly overstates the penalty, and dirt is the only surface here that actually costs road wheels time. From September the monthly series also carries Crit Club, Epic Race Club and TT Club events alongside the ZRacing stage; only the ZRacing stages are modelled here, since the stage slug convention (stage-{n}) assumes one race per week and the other three formats are separate weekly events with their own routes. If they are ever added they need their own slug convention, not a second race on the same week.

categories.label: All categories
categories.curatorNote: zwift-data's slug for Mech Isle Mayhem is the bare numeric id. ZwiftInsider's published 20.4 km ran about 2 km over route + lead-in (18.4 km) because Zwift's game dictionary publishes an 85 m lead-in for this route - the same value it gives Urumaze and a Mech Isle running route. Corrected in shared/data/routeEventLeadIns.ts from the published distance and confirmed by a Strava segment effort, so our total now matches the listing.

races.note: The month opens with a single lap of Mech Isle Mayhem - about 20 km with only 121 m of climbing, so expect a fast, draft-heavy race that stays together. Only a third of the lap is tarmac, but the 35% beach sand rolls at tarmac speed in Zwift, so road wheels still win comfortably; it's the 21% dirt that costs time. Feather and Ghost are the powerups on offer.
races.curatorNote: ZwiftInsider notes Zwift disabled racing-score changes for this stage due to finish line inaccuracies - a results detail, not an equipment one, so it stays out of the rider-facing note.

categories.label: All categories
categories.curatorNote: Same route ZRL 2026/27 R1W3 gives C/D - zwift-data's numeric id is the real slug. The published 26.8 km exceeds route + lead-in for the same reason as stage 1, and is corrected in shared/data/routeEventLeadIns.ts; 152 real finishers reproduce at +1.07% on the corrected distance against -5.78% on the uncorrected one.

races.note: Urumaze is a clean, rolling lap where ordinary road aero wins - the 202 m of climbing never bites hard enough to hand the race to a lightweight build. Two fifths of the lap is beach sand, which sounds slow and isn't: Zwift rolls sand at tarmac Crr, so it costs road wheels nothing. Feather and Aero powerups.

categories.label: All categories
categories.curatorNote: ZwiftInsider styles the name "WhatYumeziWe'reLost?"; zwift-data (and the game) spell it WhatYumeziWereLost. Published figures match route + lead-in within 1%.

races.note: The hilliest stage of the month: 288 m of climbing packed into under 18 km, over twice the gradient density of the other three stages. This is the week where climbing performance genuinely matters, and the Feather powerup doubles down on it. It is also the dirtiest stage - a quarter of the route is dirt, the surface that hurts road wheels most here, though not enough to beat them. Draft is the other powerup.

categories.label: All categories
categories.curatorNote: zwift-data's numeric id is the real slug; the route is a 3.9 km lap circuit, and 5 laps + lead-in comes to 19.6 km against ZwiftInsider's published 21.2 km - the same ~2 km event-pen overshoot as stages 1 and 2.

races.note: The month closes with a crit: five laps of the 3.9 km Twilight Crit circuit, near-flat and relentlessly fast. Over 40% of each lap is brick, which is bumpy to look at but barely slower than tarmac on road wheels - this stays a pure aero race. With Draft and Aero as the powerups, the equipment and the powerups are pulling in the same direction.

rounds.name: September: Zwift Racing Powered by DURA-ACE

categories.label: All categories
categories.curatorNote: Two laps plus the 3.2 km France lead-in comes to 21.8 km, matching the published distance exactly - no lead-in correction needed. The published 122 m looks high against two laps of the route's own 49 m until the lead-in's 23 m is added: 49x2 + 23 = 121 m. Both figures confirm the mapping.

races.note: The month opens in France with two laps of Croissant: 21.8 km of unbroken tarmac and only 122 m of climbing, none of it steep. Nothing on this course rewards a light bike, so it is a flat-out aero race - and with Aero and Draft as the powerups, the field should stay bunched and fast to the line.

categories.label: All categories
categories.curatorNote: Route plus lead-in is 19.25 km against the published 19.2 km, and the elevation matches exactly - a normal Watopia route with a real 193 m lead-in, so none of the round-8 event-pen overshoot applies.

races.note: A single lap of Watopia's Ocean Lava Cliffside Loop - 19.2 km with 156 m of climbing spread thinly rather than stacked into one wall. Nine tenths of the lap is tarmac, and the short dirt, wood and cobble stretches together come to under 2 km, not enough to pull the answer away from road wheels. Feather and Anvil are the powerups.

categories.label: All categories
categories.curatorNote: Point-to-point, so laps is 1 by definition. Route plus lead-in is 19.6 km, matching the published distance - unlike the Makuri event-only routes in round 8, this one's lead-in needs no correction. Published elevation is 204 m against the route's own 190 m, inside the validator's threshold and left as published.

races.note: Back to Makuri for Electric Break, a point-to-point that packs 204 m into 19.6 km - the sharpest climbing of the month so far. Only a third of it is tarmac, but that reads worse than it rides: the 36% beach sand rolls at tarmac rolling resistance in Zwift and costs road wheels nothing, the 29% brick is barely slower, and only 3% is dirt, the one surface here that actually bites. So it stays an aero race with a climb in it. Feather and Aero powerups.

categories.label: All categories
categories.curatorNote: Watopia's Loop de Loop, not Paris' Loop de loop de loop - two laps plus lead-in is 25.0 km and 288 m against the published 25 km and 289 m, so the mapping is confirmed by both figures.

races.note: The month closes with two laps of Watopia's Loop de Loop: 25 km and 289 m, the most climbing of the four stages, though at under 12 m per kilometre it is rolling rather than mountainous. The lap is almost entirely tarmac, so surfaces are a non-issue and the whole question is how much the climbs claw back from a full aero build. Feather and Anvil again.
